classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the staircase's horizontal and vertical segments sum to the given total width and height.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of the figure below. All angles are right angles.

spec.description: Unshaded closed orthogonal staircase with four rightward segments alternating with four downward segments. The full left side and full bottom side are each labelled 10 m. Drawing coordinates preserve the source silhouette without assigning individual step lengths.
spec.mathematics: The rightward staircase segments together equal the total width of 10 m; the downward staircase segments together equal the total height of 10 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two supplied 10 m labels appear; totals for the staircase and the perimeter are solution-only.

answer.short:
$40\text{ m}$

The horizontal steps total $10\text{ m}$, and the vertical steps total $10\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
The horizontal steps together equal the bottom side, $10\text{ m}$. The vertical steps together equal the left side, $10\text{ m}$. Add all the boundary lengths:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Perimeter}&=10+10+10+10\\\text{Perimeter}&=40\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
